pattern: bought during the marriage is marital property
struck: In South Carolina, a house bought during the marriage is marital property even if only one spouse's name is on the deed.
use: In South Carolina, a house bought during the marriage is usually marital property, even if only one spouse's name is on the deed. The exceptions include a house bought with one spouse's inherited or premarital money, or one a prenuptial agreement leaves out.

pattern: owned before the marriage stays (?:theirs|his|hers|yours|separate)
struck: A house one spouse owned before the marriage stays theirs, but any rise in its value that came from the other spouse's efforts can be divided.
use: A house one spouse owned before the marriage is not marital property under the law, but any rise in its value that came from the other spouse's efforts can be divided.

pattern: once (?:it|the notice|that notice) is filed,? it does
struck: Until that notice is filed, a spouse's claim does not bind a buyer or lender; once it is filed, it does.
use: After the notice is filed, a buyer or lender who takes an interest later is bound by the case. It does not affect a lender or buyer whose rights came before it.

pattern: (?:cannot|can't|may not) grant a final divorce (?:until|before) three months
struck: The court cannot grant a final divorce until three months after the case is filed.
use: On most grounds a final divorce cannot be granted until three months after the case is filed. On the one-year-apart ground, the divorce can be granted once the other spouse has answered or is in default.

pattern: contested issues[^.]{0,100}\bgo to (?:court-ordered )?mediation
struck: Contested issues in a divorce case, the house included, go to court-ordered mediation in South Carolina.
use: Most contested issues in a divorce case, the house included, must go to mediation, unless the case is exempt or the spouses agree to arbitration or early neutral evaluation instead.

pattern: \bboth (?:spouses |owners )?(?:must )?sign the listing
struck: When both spouses own it, both sign the listing.
use: When a husband and wife own the house together, we have both sign the listing.

pattern: change[s]? to an accepted (?:deal|offer|contract)[^.]{0,80}initial
struck: Any change to an accepted deal is in writing and initialed by both sides.
use: Changes made during negotiations are in writing, initialed and dated by both sides.

pattern: until (?:they|you|the spouses|both|the two)[^.]{0,20} agree in writing
struck: The closing attorney must keep the disputed part in trust until they agree in writing or a court decides.
use: The closing attorney must keep the disputed part separate until they agree, a court decides, or a narrow exception in the rule applies.

pattern: \bqualif\w*[^.]{0,40}\b(?:alone|on (?:their|your|his|her) own)\b
struck: The spouse who keeps the house gets none of the cash and must qualify for the loan alone.
use: The spouse who keeps the house gets none of the cash and must qualify for the new loan under Fannie Mae's rules.

pattern: buyout is (?:often|usually|typically) paid
struck: A buyout is often paid with a new loan.
use: A buyout can be paid with a new loan.

pattern: lender (?:cannot|can't|may not) (?:demand|call)[^.]{0,140}(?:divorce|settlement)
struck: A lender cannot demand the whole loan be paid because a divorce decree or property settlement moves the house to the borrower's spouse.
use: A lender cannot demand the whole loan be paid because a divorce decree moves a home of one to four units to the borrower's spouse, when the borrower lived in it and the spouse who gets it lives there.

pattern: buyout deed saves
struck: On the middle $350,000 house, a buyout deed saves the $1,295 a sale would cost.
use: A buyout deed pays no deed fee; a sale of the same $350,000 house pays $1,295.

pattern: time away counts against
struck: Without such a paper, time away counts against the spouse who left.
use: Without one of those papers, the time after you move out does not count as time you lived there.

pattern: count the time the other spouse owned it
struck: The spouse who keeps the house takes over the old cost basis, and can count the time the other spouse owned it.
use: The spouse who keeps the house takes over the old cost basis and can count the time the other spouse owned it, but must meet the 2-year living-there test on their own.

pattern: married if your divorce is not final by December 31
struck: For the tax year, you are married if your divorce is not final by December 31, even if you live apart.
use: If you have no final decree of divorce or separate maintenance by December 31, you count as married for that whole year, even if you live apart.

pattern: before the closing attorney'?s fee
struck: Each gets about $74,350 less $1,750 for each 1 percent of fees, before the closing attorney's fee.
use: Each gets about $74,350 less $1,750 for each 1 percent of agent fees, before the closing attorney's fee and other closing costs.

pattern: until the old loan is paid off,? both
struck: Until the old loan is paid off, both owe it.
use: Until the old loan is paid off or the lender releases the other spouse, both owe it.

pattern: tracks repeat sales of the same
struck: The index tracks repeat sales of the same single-family houses with Fannie Mae or Freddie Mac loans.
use: The index tracks repeat sales and refinance appraisals of the same single-family houses with Fannie Mae or Freddie Mac loans.

pattern: since (?:mid-|the middle of )?1996
struck: The whole gain stays under one person's $250,000 limit for any house bought since mid-1996.
use: For a typical house bought in 1998 or later, the estimated gain is under one person's $250,000 limit.

pattern: filed in the county where the other spouse lives,? or where
struck: A divorce case is filed in the county where the other spouse lives, or where the couple last lived together.
use: A divorce case is heard in the county where the spouse being sued lives; where the spouse filing lives, if the other lives out of state or cannot be found; or where the couple last lived together, unless the spouse filing lives out of state.

pattern: Clerk of Court[^.]{0,80}\bis at 1301
struck: In Horry County, the Clerk of Court for the Circuit and Family Court is at 1301 Second Avenue in Conway.
use: Horry County's Clerk of Court for the Circuit and Family Court has its main office at 1301 Second Avenue in Conway and a second office at 332 Hinson Drive in Myrtle Beach.

pattern: \ba sale does not pay off the loan
struck: Then a sale does not pay off the loan.
use: Then the money from a sale would not pay off the loan.

pattern: (?:lender would have to agree|would need the lender to agree)[^.]{0,40}short sale
struck: The lender would have to agree to a short sale, a sale for less than what is owed. / A sale would need the lender to agree to a short sale.
use: The lender may agree to a short sale, a sale for less than what is owed.

pattern: names are on the deed, no\b
struck: If both of your names are on the deed, no.
use: If both of your names are on the deed, your spouse cannot sell the whole house without you. A deed signed by one spouse passes no more than that spouse's share.
